direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is surrealist and funny to create this dry comedy that makes you question what you are watching; the direction on a microscale is pretty funny with how silly and absurdist it is, but also still makes you wonder what you are watching; Spike Jonze's  storytelling perfectly complements Charlie Kaufman's quirky and unique writing to create this surrealist and imaginative world that makes you question what it means to be alive and sentient

performance.comments: Plays this dorky character that has good chemistry with the cast as he tries to impress Keener, despite his relationship with Diaz; has good chemistry with the cast

Plays a performance very atypical to her filmography as she is this neurotic and anxious wife who is very unsure of her marriage with Cusack as she becomes enamored with Keener; has good chemistry with the cast

The best performance in the cast as she presents comedic, seductive, and persuasive tones to create a character that people are drawn to, for different reasons; has very good chemistry with Cusack and Diaz
Plays himself well as he is merely a vessel for the plot to move forward

cast.comments: Everybody plays their role well and has good chemistry with each other

story.comments: The concept is very unique and interesting, maybe even a little too unique, as it explores what it means to be alive in such a surrealist and absurdist way; the plot structure is pretty linear and straightforward; character writing is pretty good as it definitely paints caricatures that help move the plot forward, with Keener's character being the best written

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty silly and funny, while also being profound in its discussion of philosophy; the humor is very dry and absurdist, and helps add to the silly comedy of this movie; the symbolism is very strong and meaningful as it touches on themes of what it means to be human; the foreshadowing is pretty standard

cinematography.comments: Uses a lot of forced perspective and and movie magic to help add to the surrealist and absurdist tone of the movie

editing.comments: Helps add ot the surrealist and absurdist tone of the movie; has a lot of late 90s editing techniques that feel a bit dated

visual_effects.comments: Uses a lot of practical effects to emulate the puppeteering nature of the movie; uses a lot of forced perspective and movie magic to help add to the surrealist and absurdist tone of the movie; has a lot of late 90s effects that feel a bit dated

production_design.comments: The office adds to the silly nature of the movie and uses a lot of forced perspective to help with the effects of the movie

review.pacing: Pacing is pretty good for the most part, but kinda drags in the second half
review.tone: Tone is very surrealist and absurdist to create this silly comedy that has signature traits of both Spike Jonze and Charlie Kaufman
review.overall: Overall, this marks a strong feature directorial and written debut from Spike Jonze and Charlie Kaufman, showcasing their signature absurdist and surrealist styles; this silly comedy successfully creates a thought-provoking narrative that touches on identity and what it means to be sentient
